description: Flee is an agent-based modelling toolkit for simulating the movement of individuals across geographical locations, used mainly to forecast the movements of forcibly displaced persons fleeing conflict towards towns and refugee camps. Agents move over a location graph of conflict zones, towns and camps connected by routes of known length, following movement rules that respond to conflict events, distance and camp capacity; extensions add food security from IPC data, weather coupling and multiscale coupling of micro and macro models. Derek Groen's group at Brunel University London develops it, with funding from the EU Horizon 2020 projects HiDALGO and VECMA, and its publications validate it against historical refugee arrivals. Coverage is any region for which a location graph and conflict data are built; resolution is the individual agent and one day. It is Python code on GitHub (release tags up to v3.1, v3.2 beta) with MPI parallelism and the FabFlee plugin for automated input construction and remote execution on supercomputers. Licence: BSD-style (Brunel University London), free. Caveats: building a location graph and calibrating movement rules for a new conflict is substantial work, and forecasts depend on conflict scenarios. Simulation uses: agent-based forecasting of displacement for emergency response planning, including the capacity of camps and of the food, health and shelter services that receive displaced people. Related records: none catalogued yet; IPC food security data is listed in the register.
inputs: Location graph of conflict zones, towns and camps with route lengths
Optionally IPC food security data and weather
